video_title: “I saw a RUTHLESS side of the NBA that people don’t talk about!” | David Roddy

quotes.speaker: David Roddy
quotes.summary_phrase: David Roddy on the business-driven nature of NBA trades
quotes.excerpt: if they see a piece or a player somewhere else that might have better numbers, they're going to try to trade
quotes.quote: There's many reasons. I had a great time in Memphis and I was playing a lot of minutes and I ended up getting traded pretty much after that. That opportunity was gone. So if they see a piece or a player somewhere else that might have better numbers, they're going to try to trade for that player.

quotes.speaker: David Roddy
quotes.summary_phrase: David Roddy defends Ja Morant against media narrative
quotes.excerpt: I think the media has Ja Morant, his image, completely wrong. He's a great leader.

text_blocks.speaker: Sasa Obradovic
text_blocks.text: You played in Memphis with another player which is Ja Morant. We know all the stories that happened to him. What's your perspective on Ja Morant?

text_blocks.speaker: David Roddy
text_blocks.text: First and foremost, I think the media has Ja Morant, his image, completely wrong. He's a great leader. He took all of our rookies under his wing and he just has an amazing heart.

quotes.speaker: David Roddy
quotes.summary_phrase: David Roddy's championship objectives with Hapoel Jerusalem
quotes.excerpt: The objective is to win everything. Win all the cups, win the EuroCup, and get promoted to the EuroLeague.
quotes.quote: The objective is to win everything. Win all the cups, win the EuroCup, and get promoted to the EuroLeague. That's the reason why all of us are here. Matan and Dan and Coach Sasa have all believed in us and believed in me. That's what we're here to do.

quotes.speaker: David Roddy
quotes.summary_phrase: David Roddy explains the business side of NBA roster management
quotes.excerpt: everyone is looking for the right result. Everyone's trying to win a championship or they're trying to build their future
quotes.quote: The NBA is a business in many ways. Everyone is looking for the right result. Everyone's trying to win a championship or they're trying to build their future to win a championship. And sometimes the chemistry on a team is the best that it can be, everyone is young, everyone's thriving, but the business side is that someone is trying to win a championship. So if they see a piece or a player somewhere else that might have better numbers, might have a better look on paper with analytics and everything that's going on in the NBA, they're going to try to trade for that player or get picks for that player.

quotes.speaker: David Roddy
quotes.summary_phrase: David Roddy on the importance of being a professional in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: that's why they pay them the big bucks, is to be a professional.
quotes.quote: Absolutely, you can improve. I think that's why they pay them the big bucks, is to be a professional. One of the cliche sayings that they always say, veterans to young players is, be a pro. In the moment you don't want to hear it, but it just encompasses everything that it takes to be an NBA player. You can be starting or playing 25 minutes a game for a month and then someone comes back from injury and you're not playing for the next 10 games. So in that 10 games, are you going to just relax and go party and just lay around until you play again, or are you going to attack this time where you can actually work on your game?

quotes.speaker: David Roddy
quotes.summary_phrase: David Roddy on the habits required to reach the NBA
quotes.excerpt: if you're struggling to show up on time to practice or treatment, if you're not showing respect to the trainers
quotes.quote: It takes a lot. It takes a lot. A little bit of luck, absolutely, just with the situation that you're in. So many college guys have NBA talent or potential, but you really have to apply the habits early. So if you're struggling to show up on time to practice or treatment, or if you're not showing respect to the trainers and the coaches and you're not coachable, then you have no chance to be in the NBA. So all of those habits have to start first, and then after that, you just really just work and just trust the process.

quotes.speaker: David Roddy
quotes.summary_phrase: David Roddy recounts the intense pre-draft workout process
quotes.excerpt: I was scheduled to do 16 workouts. In eight weeks, I did 16.
quotes.quote: The pre-draft process was crazy for me. I was scheduled to do 16 workouts. In eight weeks, I did 16. And then I decided to stay in the draft June 1st. So basically within 20 days, I probably did about 12.

quotes.speaker: David Roddy
quotes.summary_phrase: David Roddy on his first NBA game against the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: I looked at who was guarding me, and it was my childhood hero, Derrick Rose.
quotes.quote: The very first game we played the Knicks at home, and I had no idea I was going to get subbed in the game or not. It was a nationally televised game, the Knicks had Jalen Brunson, Julius Randle, and I got subbed in the game and I couldn't hear anything. Once I got to my spot, I looked at who was guarding me, and it was my childhood hero, Derrick Rose. So he subbed in at the same time. So I just froze in time for a moment. I was like, yo, this is pretty crazy.

quotes.speaker: David Roddy
quotes.summary_phrase: David Roddy on guarding Luka Doncic
quotes.excerpt: Luka gave us 40, and he gave me like 21 points in like seven minutes.
quotes.quote: My real NBA moment was my third game against Dallas against Luka. So Luka gave us 40, and he gave me like 21 points in like seven minutes. I was guarding him. Yeah, so that was my first time guarding a point guard, so I didn't know how to guard a double drag and he just kept coming off the double drag to want a lob or making scoring a basket.

quotes.speaker: David Roddy
quotes.summary_phrase: David Roddy on underrated NBA players like Derrick White
quotes.excerpt: Derrick White, for example, like one of the first times that I played Derrick White
quotes.quote: Like Derrick White, for example, like one of the first times that I played Derrick White, he gave us like 25 points, but it was just off of catch and shoot threes or just making the right play at all times. Those types of guys are always annoying to play against.

quotes.speaker: David Roddy
quotes.summary_phrase: David Roddy on Ja Morant's leadership and character
quotes.excerpt: He took all of our rookies under his wing, my first year. And he just has an amazing heart.
quotes.quote: First and foremost, I think the media has Ja Morant, his image, completely wrong. He's a great leader. He was vocal from the jump. He took all of our rookies under his wing, my first year. And he just has an amazing heart. People don't really, people misunderstand him a lot. It's very easy just because, you know, he's young, he makes mistakes just like everybody else, but people are trying to bash it over his head continually.

quotes.speaker: David Roddy
quotes.summary_phrase: David Roddy on the difficulty of staying ready in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: I've seen it so many times where, you know, players have sat out for months
quotes.quote: It's extremely difficult. You know, I think just to stay ready is to have your mind clear and have a routine down, especially when you're not playing. So I've seen it so many times where, you know, players have sat out for months and in come playoff time, two guys are injured and now they're playing 20, 25 minutes a game.
